challenge-resolution.name: Challenge → Resolution
challenge-resolution.summary: Identify a current business challenge, trace its origins, and recommend an actionable resolution. Useful for management consulting, internal strategy memos, and any deck where the audience needs a clear path from problem to plan.

beats.name: Hook
beats.description: Open with a specific, visible signal of the challenge — a metric heading the wrong way, a customer story, a competitive event. The hook should make the audience nod that yes, this matters.

beats.name: Dilemma
beats.description: State the challenge plainly. What is failing, who is feeling it, and why has it now risen to a level that demands a decision? The dilemma must feel real, not academic.

beats.name: Backdrop
beats.description: Provide the context behind the dilemma: how it formed, what's been tried, what constraints exist. Just enough history that the audience trusts your diagnosis without drowning in detail.

beats.name: Remedy
beats.description: Propose the resolution. Lead with the recommendation, then sketch the approach. Be opinionated — vague remedies invite vague responses.

beats.name: Evidence
beats.description: Demonstrate why the remedy will work. Comparable cases, supporting data, or pilot results. Choose evidence that addresses the audience's most likely objection, not the one easiest to answer.

beats.name: Motivate
beats.description: Make the case for acting now. Quantify the cost of delay and the upside of decisive action. Help the audience picture the room a quarter from now if they say yes.

beats.name: Conclusion
beats.description: Recap the challenge, the remedy, and the specific decision you need from the audience. End with a clear ask, not a summary slide.

customer.name: Customer
customer.summary: End customers receiving product demos, onboarding presentations, or business reviews.
customer.description: Customers receiving product demos, onboarding, or business reviews. Speak in their language, focus on the value they realize, keep visuals simple, and use strong product screenshots. Keep chart density low; 10-20 slides.

internal-team.name: Internal Team
internal-team.summary: Company employees across functions receiving operational updates, project status, or training content.
internal-team.description: Employees across functions receiving operational updates, project status, or training. Make next steps, owners, and progress visible, and state action items explicitly. Moderate chart density; 10-20 slides.

persuade.name: Persuade
persuade.summary: Change belief or win support for a specific argument, idea, or recommendation.
persuade.description: Use when the audience may be skeptical or undecided. Build a crisp thesis, support it with evidence, address objections, and end with a clear action.
persuade.outcome: The audience accepts the argument or supports the recommendation.

inspirational.name: Inspirational
inspirational.summary: Aspirational, narrative-driven voice for keynotes, founders, and rallying cries.
inspirational.description: Reach for shared belief and possibility, then ground it in something concrete. Use vivid imagery and rhythm; avoid collapsing into hype by always pairing aspiration with a real anchor.
voiceCues: Open with belief; close with action.
Use rhythm — paired phrases, repetition, deliberate beats.
Pair every aspirational claim with a concrete proof point.
Speak in present tense to make the future feel inevitable.
avoid: Stacked superlatives ('the very best, world-changing, revolutionary').
Dense data tables — push numbers into supporting slides.
samplePhrases: We're building the runtime that makes agents feel instant.
When latency disappears, what becomes possible?
The next decade of software belongs to teams who treat speed as a feature.

cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

burnt-orange.description: A warm, high-contrast palette built around burnt orange, red, navy, and gold. It feels active without losing structure.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
